top5.text: Democrats are projected to have won both the House and Senate; Mississippi and Alaska are still too close to call.
Speaker Johnson won't seek GOP leader; Vance blames the Iran war for the loss.
Poland's RPP held at 3.75%; the new projection sees 2027 inflation at 3.1–5.3% if fuel caps end.

links.label: TVN24 Biznes; PAP via Portal Samorządowy

top5.text: Poland's Constitutional Tribunal split deepens as rival camps claim its leadership; Tusk and Nawrocki agree to meet.
New Delhi says the India–US interim deal is unaffected by the midterms; a Modi–Trump meeting in Manila is possible.

links.label: PTI via Siasat; The Tribune / ANI

US.text: Networks project that Democrats won both chambers. Reported Senate flips include Texas, Kansas, Iowa, Ohio, Maine and North Carolina, and CBS projects at least 54 Democratic seats.
Mississippi (Colom ahead of Hyde-Smith by about 1,100 votes) and Alaska (Peltola ahead of Sullivan by about 640) remain uncalled.
Johnson won't run for GOP leader; Scalise and Jordan are reported to be running for a Nov 10 vote. Jeffries is bidding for Speaker.
Vance blamed the Iran war for the defeat. Trump partly agreed, citing petrol prices, but said he would do it again. Fox frames this as soul-searching, NBC and the Washington Post as a rebuke.
Qatar is pushing a draft built on confidence-building steps, while Iran wants the blockade lifted first. Axios reports a US strike on Qeshm on Nov 3.
The Dow rose about 1,570 points on Nov 4 as Brent fell about 8%. Chip stocks slid on Nov 5 on fears of tougher AI regulation.
The CDC Ebola attestation for all inbound air travellers is now in force.

Poland.text: The RPP held the reference rate at 3.75%. Glapiński says no hike is decided and that inflation would be much lower if the fuel caps were extended.

links.label: TVN24 Biznes; PAP via Portal Samorządowy

Poland.text: A judges' assembly led by Korwin-Piotrowska set an 8-judge quorum, and the Święczkowski camp calls it unlawful. TVN24 and RMF say the Tribunal is working again; wPolityce calls her a 'usurper'.
After the National Security Council met, Tusk and Nawrocki agreed to a one-on-one meeting; no date is set.
The government resubmitted the PIT/CIT reform as a new bill after constitutional doubts over the Senate's amendments. It passed first reading.
A Senate committee advanced the bill restoring abortion for severe foetal defects; the Senate votes on Nov 6.
Łukasz Pabiś was named commissioner for Częstochowa after the recall vote.
Hackers took over refrigeration controllers at Auchan stores. CERT Polska found 140 exposed devices, and the Digital Affairs Ministry threatened to name firms that don't disconnect them.

Kraków.text: The monthly resident pass returns to 90 zł, but only from Sep 2027.
Gibała wants Kraków to leave Eurocities and other associations to save about 8.2m zł a year; the city council must agree.
Kraków.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor

India.text: The Cabinet approved Rs 14,500 crore for 92 GWh of grid storage, plus lithium and nickel processing support and the 8th Economic Census.
The Supreme Court issued notice on the challenge to election commissioners' lifetime immunity. The main pleas against the CEC are likely around Nov 17.
India.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR

India.text: Siddaramaiah demanded that SIR be scrapped and that the CEC resign, claiming 99 lakh deletions in Karnataka. The figure is unverified.
India.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR

India.text: Amar Ujala reports a two-year Agniveer extension before the first batch exits on Nov 21. It is unconfirmed officially.
India launched three indigenous AI models that work in Indian languages.

city.text: The S52 Dziekanowice tunnel is closed tonight 21:00–05:00 for safety tests; detours via DW772 and al. 29 Listopada.
Trams were back on normal routes after Wednesday's overhead-wire break.
Moderate: PM2.5 about 11.5 µg/m³ at 18:00 (IQAir). No smog alert. GIOŚ data could not be reached.
An IMGW first-degree dense-fog warning ran until 10:00 today; watch for rime and slippery roads overnight.
11 Nov: the Independence Run starts 11:11 at Bulwar Czerwieński, and Wawel entry is free 9:00–17:00 with an online ticket. Wawel's state rooms are free all November.

US–Poland.text: PiS's Błaszczak says the Democratic win kills the permanent US base; Warsaw still expects a decision in December.

US–India.text: Officials say the interim deal needs no Congressional approval. Analysts are split on whether a weakened Trump speeds it up.

links.label: PTI via Siasat; The Tribune / ANI

US–India.text: A Modi–Trump meeting at the ASEAN summit in Manila is possible, per a single source.
CERT-In reportedly has access to Anthropic's Mythos for critical-systems security. (This desk is produced with Anthropic's Claude.)

Poland–India.text: Jitin Prasada's 12-company delegation discussed AI, chips and minerals in Warsaw; no agreements were signed.

rules.name: Order: Requirement for Attestation for All Airline or Other Aircraft Passengers Arriving in the United States (Ebola, DRC)
rules.changes: Every international air passenger to or through the US must attest to no presence in DR Congo in the past 21 days; airlines must deny boarding without the attestation.
rules.affects: All international air travellers to the US, including from Poland and India, and airlines.

rules.name: Bill amending PIT and CIT (2027 tax reform, resubmitted)
rules.changes: Raises the PIT threshold to 130k zł, adds a 24% band for 130–150k zł and 32% above that, raises the solidarity levy to 5%, sets 22% CIT for firms with revenue above €50m (banks excluded) and cuts the lump-sum tax revenue limit to €250k.
rules.affects: Higher earners, large companies and the self-employed on the lump-sum tax.

rules.name: Order cutting the residents' monthly network ticket to 90 zł (zarządzenie)
rules.changes: The residents' monthly pass for the whole network falls from 99 zł to 90 zł.
rules.affects: Kraków residents who buy monthly passes; they save 9 zł a month from Sep 2027.

rules.name: Viability Gap Funding scheme for grid-scale energy storage (2026-27 to 2030-31)
rules.changes: Rs 14,500 crore of central support for 92 GWh of storage (60 GWh pumped hydro, 30 GWh battery), awarded by tariff-based bidding, with 40% domestic content required for battery projects. Detailed guidelines are not yet notified.
rules.affects: Power distribution companies, storage developers and battery makers.

deepDive.title: Hacked fridges, frontier AI and a voter backlash
deepDive.body:
Technology turned up in an unusual place in all three countries this week: at the ballot box, in supermarket freezers, and in a national cyber agency's toolkit.

**Poland.** Hackers took remote control of refrigeration controllers and heated units at three Auchan stores, a small grocery and a food distributor, spoiling stock (Confirmed). It is part of a wave that hit about 700 stores in France and more in Belgium, Sweden and Luxembourg. CERT Polska found 140 devices exposed to the internet. Deputy PM Gawkowski told firms to disconnect them or be publicly named, and GIS told food businesses to check temperatures by hand. Pro-Kremlin groups claimed some attacks; analysts say the methods were simple (weak passwords, old flaws) and the claims are unproven ([Salon24/money.pl](https://www.salon24.pl/newsroom/1531587,cyberatak-na-lodowki-rzad-wydal-rekomendacje-firmom)).

**US.** Analysts argue that a backlash against Big Tech and data centres helped Democrats win (Reported, analysis). Chipmakers fell sharply on Nov 5 on fears of tougher AI rules. But Democrats take the committee gavels only in January, and Trump's veto points to gridlock rather than reversal ([The National](https://thenationalnews.com/future/technology/2026/11/05/data-center-bans-industrial-stocks-ai)).

**India.** CERT-In has reportedly been given Anthropic's restricted Mythos model to probe critical systems, after months of talks (Reported; this desk is produced with Claude). Three home-grown models that work in Indian languages launched this week. The consent-manager phase of the data-protection rules starts on Nov 13, and MeitY's promised AI consultation paper on deepfakes and safety is now overdue ([ThePrint](https://theprint.in/india/governance/india-steps-up-ai-regulation-push-with-consultation-paper-likely-next-month-deepfakes-safety-in-focus/3065386/)).

**Poland–India.** Gawkowski, who is also leading the fridge response, hosted India's Jitin Prasada for talks on AI, chips and data centres.

**What to watch:** Polish attribution of the attacks, the consent-manager launch on Nov 13, and the incoming House's first bills on data centres and AI-chip exports.
